Grid search: every entry, exit and filter setting

Residual-beta project, Phase B2 · 31 pairs · settings chosen in-sample on 2016-2022, scored out of sample on 2023-2026 · one tab per bar size · 2026-09-25

Each bar size has its own grid: 735 settings per pair at daily, 784 intraday. The heatmaps show the shape of the entry-by-exit space; the table lists every setting with its median in-sample and out-of-sample scores across pairs, sortable and filterable; the last table shows one pair's top settings. Green cells clear the plan's 0.8 bar; amber is 0.3-0.8; red is negative.

Ranked across all bar sizes: what has the best chance of panning out

Rank = the worse of the in-sample (2016-22) and out-of-sample (2023-26) net Sharpe, so a strategy only ranks high if it worked in both windows. Only settings positive in both windows are listed, with at least the minimum in-sample trade count. Costs are one half-spread per leg on every position change.

Settings judged across all their pairs

One row = one setting applied to every sector (11) or every sleeve (20) at one bar size. This is the honest list: no pair was chosen.

Best chance of panning out

Across all pairs, nothing clears the bar. The best setting held in both windows is Daily mean reversion on sectors (W=60,entry=1.5,exit=0.5,stop=4,vollo): in-sample +0.26, out-of-sample +0.29, positive on 73% of pairs. That is a market-neutral book earning a Sharpe of about 0.3, not a strategy.

Among single pairs, the survivors are almost all daily (23 of the top 30), low-turnover (mostly 5-15 trades a year) and concentrated in the defensive sectors (XLP, XLRE, XLU) and a few sleeves (IHI, JETS), where costs are irrelevant and the residual is largest. A worse-of-two-windows Sharpe of 0.6-0.8 on ten to forty test trades is the most any of this research supports, and with 31 pairs, 784 settings and four bar sizes behind the search it is within what chance produces. If one thing were to be carried forward, it is the daily sector mean-reversion book (60-day window, enter at |z| of 1.5-2, exit at 0.5, calm-volatility regimes), run as a paper portfolio across all eleven sectors rather than the pairs that happened to win, and judged on a fresh window. Expect a Sharpe near 0.3, market-neutral.
